scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: `pkg/sessiontxn` is ported as `tidb-sessiontxn` (2026-11-19): `TxnManager` holds one provider per transaction (`Optimistic`, `PessimisticRR`, `PessimisticRC`, `PessimisticSerializable`, `StalenessTxnContextProvider`, chosen as `newProviderWithRequest`), which owns the transaction and answers each statement's snapshot, `OnStmtStart` (RCCheckTS), `OnStmtRetry` (the for-update timestamp) and `OnStmtErrorForNextAction` (pessimistic lock errors, the after-query retry). Remaining: (1) the statement lifecycle opens the statement's snapshot before it compiles (`with_bound_statement` -> `open_read_snapshot` -> `run`), where Go compiles, advises (`AdviseOptimizeWithPlan`), builds (activating the transaction) and then reads; so the optimistic provider's max-ts point get is decided from the AST (`classify.rs` `statement_read_shape_bound` -> `AutocommitPointGet`, `open_read_snapshot`'s arm) instead of from the plan (`IsPointGetWithPKOrUniqueKeyByAutoCommit`); (2) Go enters every transaction through `TxnManager.EnterNewTxn(request)` -> `newProviderWithRequest` -> `OnInitialize`, while `TxnManager` has one entry per case (`open`, `enter_pending`, `enter_implicit_write` / `_read`, `enter_stale`) that builds the transaction before the provider wraps it (`decide_txn_mode` itself runs where Go's `PrepareTxnCtx` runs it). (Done 2026-11-20: a statement's fresh for-update timestamp is fetched when the builder asks, `stmt_for_update_ts` on the statement's store, as Go's `getForUpdateTs`; `TestMaterializedViewRefreshCompleteOutOfPlaceConcurrentChildFast` runs.)

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: `mysql.*` tables have two access paths. Go reads and writes every system table through SQL on an internal session (`ExecRestrictedSQL` / `sess.Execute`): the DDL job queue, DDL history, reorg handles, delete ranges, the MDL info, the privilege load (`cache.go` `LoadAll`), `mysql.global_variables`, the statistics tables and the bootstrap rows. This port also has a direct key/value reader and writer, `tidb-syssession`'s `SystemTableView` (`mysql_system_tables.rs`) and `system_row_write.rs`, which decode and encode rows through `TableCommon` with their own default materialization, casting and handle-layout choice (`HandleLayout::of`). The DDL's production steps already run Go's SQL (every job step has a session) and the MDL check reads `mysql.tidb_mdl_info` through SQL; the DDL tables' row encoders (`plan_insert_attempt`, `finish_ddl_job`, the `get_ddl_reorg_handle` fallback, `DdlHistoryTable`) are still reached by the session-less planning mode `tidb-ddl/tests`, `tidb-session/tests` and the bootstrap planner's tests use. No production caller is left on the direct path (re-checked 2026-11-22 against every non-test use of `scan_system_table`, `SystemRow::parse*` and `system_row_write`): the startup read of `mysql.tidb` is Go's `initGlobalVarFromSystemDB` -- a separate, unstarted domain whose session runs `getTableValue` for `system_tz` and `loadCollationParameter`, which the port did not load at all before (a store bootstrapped with new collations off ran with them on) -- and the snapshot reader `real_tikv_privileges.rs` is gone. The bootstrap is off it: `checkBootstrapped` runs Go's `USE mysql` and `getTiDBVar` on the bootstrap session (2026-11-21), and every bootstrap -- the server's and the in-process one the tests' store image is built from -- runs Go's `insertBuiltinBindInfoRow` and `doDMLWorks` statements on its bootstrap domain's session (2026-11-22), leaving `mysql_bootstrap/rows.rs`' seed rows to the fixture planner `tidb-session/tests` pin. Off it: the privilege load (both `Handle.UpdateAll` sites read through `SqlPrivilegeTables`, Go `loadTable`'s statements), the system variables (the cache reads `mysql.global_variables` with Go's `fetchTableValues` statement and writes go through SQL), the statistics save (`cluster_stats_write.rs` builds Go's four statements) and ANALYZE, and the bindings. The direct readers and writers those used to call -- `load_cluster_privileges` and `stats_table_rows`' row plans -- are now reached by tests only, a second implementation to delete with the tests that pin it (`cluster_sysvar_load.rs` / `cluster_sysvar_write.rs` are deleted, 2026-11-22). Whatever the SQL layer does on Go's path (request source and resource group, assertions, constraint checks, statement memory, `tidb_txn_assertion_level`) has to be repeated or is missing on the direct one.
findings.rust_evidence: `rust/crates/tidb-syssession/src/mysql_system_tables.rs`, `system_row_write.rs`, and the callers named in the gap

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: The test tier still runs beside the store-backed one. `tidb-kv`'s `MemTableStorage` (no transaction, `do_lock_keys` a no-op), `tidb-table`'s `LocalTableAutoIds` / `tidb-autoid` `LocalAutoIdStore`, `LocalSequenceCounter`, `tidb-session`'s `SharedCatalog` and `tidb-executor`'s `run_create_table_on` (a CREATE TABLE without a DDL job, compiled only under `test` / `test-util`) give the executor's tests a second storage, allocator and DDL implementation; Go has one path, `mockstore` through the same `kv.Transaction`, meta allocators and DDL jobs as production. Progress (2026-11-19): the Go-ported executor test files now run as Go's TestKit SQL in `tidb-session/tests` (one file per Go file, Go test names: join, hash join, executor issues, insert, batch point-get, `executor_test.go`, partition table, parallel apply, plan cache, seqtest prepared, `prepared_test.go`, aggregate, merge join, memtest, oomtest (over Go's `oomCapture` log core), `pkg/table` partition), and their executor copies are gone. Remaining (42 files, ~365 tests still build over `run_create_table_on` / `MemTableStorage`): `tidb-executor/src/driver/tests/*` and `tidb-executor/tests/*` (Rust-only; the SQL-visible ones move to TestKit, tier-internal ones go), `kv_table/tests*.rs`, `tests_table_part1/2` (Go `pkg/table/tables` tests that drive `AddRecord`/`IterRecords` on the session transaction -- the TestKit needs Go's `sessiontxn.NewTxn` / `Session().Txn(true)` surface), `tests_executor_part22` (`TestInsertIgnore` needs `kv.NewInjectedStore` over the session store), `tests_merge_join_in_disk` (`join_pkg_test.go`'s mock-data-source tests belong in the executor's unit tests over mock sources); then the tier itself goes.

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: A variable's Set behavior now lives on the variable for its warnings and session fields: `SysVarDef` carries Go's `Validation` (with a `VarsContext` for sibling reads and statement warnings), `set_session` and `set_global` hooks; `set_hooks.rs`'s deprecation-warning switch, the prune-mode / MPP-compression / hashagg-spill hooks, `tidb_enforce_mpp` and plan-replayer checks, and `SessionVars::set_session_from_hook`'s thirty typed-field branches moved onto their variables (2026-11-19). Also on their variables now (2026-11-19 late): `checkIsolationLevel`, `checkReadOnly` (the noop-gated ON switches), `max_allowed_packet`'s SET-only read-only refusal and `require_secure_transport`'s TLS / SEM refusal, through a `VarsContext` that carries Go's `vars` (the session's values in every scope, the statement type, the TLS state). Each variable has one `SetGlobal`, run on the validated value before the store for GLOBAL and INSTANCE writes as Go's `SetGlobalFromHook` is: its own (`tidb_schema_cache_size`, `tidb_redact_log`) or the one the node registers for it (the GC, MV-service and MDL switches, Go's `RegisterSysVar` from another package). Go's `GetSession` is on `SysVarDef` too (2026-11-19 night): the session-state reads (`timestamp`, `warning_count`, `error_count`, `last_insert_id` / `identity`, `tidb_current_ts` over `TxnCtx.StartTS` now on `SessionVars`, `tidb_last_txn_info` / `_query_info` / `_ddl_info`, `last_plan_from_cache` / `_binding`, `last_sql_use_alloc`, `rand_seed1` / `2`, `tidb_last_plan_replayer_token`) answer every session read -- `@@x`, `SHOW VARIABLES`, the variable tables -- where three name switches answered some surfaces (`SHOW VARIABLES` reported `warning_count` 0 and `timestamp` 0). `GetGlobal` is on `SysVarDef` as well, `global_get_hook` dispatching on it (the LDAP variables read their impls; the bind passwords read back masked, while `mysql.global_variables` keeps the value). Thirty-one `vardef`-backed variables (the TTL knobs, the DDL reorg and flashback knobs, the foreign-key / checksum / check-constraint / fast-reorg / auto-analyze / instance-plan-cache / fast-create-table switches, connection and memory limits, ...) carry Go's `SetGlobal` and `GetGlobal` over their process state, and the domain's `apply_set_global_hook` runs each variable's own `SetGlobal` first (2026-11-19 late night). So do 13 more (the OOM action, the alarm ratio, the force priority, the TiKV client's commit batch size and store limit, `require_secure_transport`, `tidb_check_mb4_value_in_utf8`, the service scope, resource control, the TTL window bounds, the reserved percentage and the PD circuit-breaker ratio, with Go's formatting and range refusals). So do the analyze default buckets / TopN, the auto-analyze priority queue, `tidb_enable_ts_validation`, the committer concurrency, `tidb_schema_cache_size` (with Go's origin text) and `tidb_redact_log`'s process-wide redaction (2026-11-19 night). The PD client options call Go's `variable.SetPDClientDynamicOption` / `SetLowResolutionTSOUpdateInterval` slots, which the domain fills (`initDomainSysVars`) and which store `vardef`'s values their `GetGlobal` read (2026-11-19 night). The statement-summary variables call `stmtsummaryv2`'s setters and the memory-arbitration variables set the process limit and arbitrator from their own `SetGlobal` (2026-11-19 night). The sysvar cache rebuild runs each variable's one `SetGlobal`, its own or the one registered for it (`SwitchMDL`, the MV service, the workload repository), as Go's `rebuildSysVarCache` does, so the domain's hook names no variable any more, and the live table's read answers each variable's own `GetGlobal` where the domain kept a `runtime_global_value` name switch (2026-11-20). Fifty-three more carry Go's `GetGlobal` (and `SetGlobal` where Go has one) since 2026-11-21: the `vardef` process switches and counters (the password-validation and password-reuse knobs, the general log, `tidb_rc_read_check_ts`, pprof SQL CPU, the expensive-query / -txn and DDL slow thresholds, batch DML, noop variables, tmp-storage-on-OOM, binding usage, dist task, stats load wait / pseudo timeout, paging size, query log length, the plan cache guard ratio, analyze column options, the advancer lag limit, ...), the constant ones (`tidb_enable_column_tracking`, `tidb_opt_index_join_build_v2`, `tidb_merge_partition_stats_concurrency`, `disconnect_on_expired_password`), and the INSTANCE variables reading the instance config (the slow-log, plugin, statement-summary file, `max_connections`, `tidb_enable_ddl` / `_stats_owner`, `tidb_config`, `tidb_log_file_max_days` settings), so the domain's `runtime_instance_value` names no variable any more (it answers only an explicit `SET INSTANCE` value) and `set_global_vars` seeds the process switches from the instance config as Go's `setGlobalVars` does. `tidb_ddl_reorg_max_write_speed` carries Go's `SetGlobal` (`units.RAMInBytes`, the [0, 1 PiB] refusal, `vardef.DDLReorgMaxWriteSpeed`, which the reorg meta now reads -- a size such as `'2KB'` used to be stored unvalidated and read as 0) and `GetGlobal` with Go's `TestSetDDLReorgMaxWriteSpeed`, and Top SQL's two limits set and read `topsqlstate.GlobalState` (2026-11-21). `tidb_enable_gc_aware_memory_track` sets and reads `memory.EnableGCAwareMemoryTrack` (2026-11-21; the switch gates Go's finalizer-deferred release accounting, which has nothing to defer where memory is freed as it is released). Remaining: 14 of Go's `GetGlobal` hooks whose state belongs to a subsystem this port reaches through a node slot or lacks (the GOGC tuner and server memory limit texts, the memory arbitrator texts, `tidb_mem_quota_analyze` -- Go's is the limit of a process-wide `GlobalAnalyzeMemoryTracker`, where this port's ANALYZE reads the variable per statement --, `tidb_external_ts`, `tidb_trace_event` -- Go re-marshals the recorder's configuration, where a missing `enabled_categories` is `null` --, the slow-log rules and rate limiter, the embedding API base), and the new process switches' readers still read the global table; Go's other `GetSession` hooks read typed fields this port keeps only in `systems`; (fixed 2026-11-19 late night: a session's load of the global session cache and the restore of a statement-scoped write run each variable's `SetSession` -- Go's `SetSystemVarWithRelaxedValidation` / `SetSystemVar` -- where 26 `*_from_systems` re-derivations and a charset/collation pairing function stood; the pairing is the six charset and collation variables' own `SetSession`); `autocommit`'s `SetSession` ending the transaction stays in `tidb-session` `variables.rs`, because Go's `SetInTxn` flag is transaction state this port keeps on the session (the `rand_seed` generator is `SessionVars.Rng` with its `SetSession` hooks, 2026-11-19 late night); (`tidb-exprstatic` loads its system variables into a real `SessionVars` through `SetSystemVar`, as Go's `newSessionVarsWithSystemVariables` does, since 2026-11-19 late night; `StaticSessionVars` is gone.)

Materialized views are ported up to their statements (phases in `rust/docs/go-shape-refactors-execplan.md`): `TableInfo` keeps Go master's `materialized_view*` fields byte for byte, the base table's DML writes its MV log rows as Go's does, the action types, schema diffs and `tidb_mview_*` / `tidb_mlog_*` variables are Go master's, and the parser takes every materialized view statement (CREATE / ALTER / DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW [LOG], REFRESH, PURGE, CANCEL, COMPARE, the SHOW forms) with Go master's restore text and syntax errors. `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG`, `DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG` and `ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG` (PURGE and ADD COLUMN) run as Go master's do, DROP / TRUNCATE / RENAME TABLE, ALTER TABLE, CREATE / DROP / ALTER INDEX, PARTITION BY, REMOVE PARTITIONING and EXCHANGE PARTITION refuse a log and its base table as Go master's do, MODIFY / CHANGE COLUMN of a logged base table retypes the log's tracked column and its dependent views' direct output columns, through their own logs and nested views, as Go master's does (`validateDependentMaterializedViewModifyColumn`, `analyzeMVColumnUsage`; a failed batched multi-schema sub-job discards the whole step and the batch's diff lists every related table, `105be7054c5`), (the log table Go builds, the base table's `MaterializedViewBase`, the `mysql.tidb_mlog_purge_info` row with its schedule, Go's refusals and the `tidb_mview_enable` gate); on a base table that is itself a materialized view the DDL session holds the view's refresh advisory lock for the job's delivery, as Go master's does. CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW runs as Go master's does: the planner's SELECT build and column count, `validateCreateMaterializedViewQuery` (via `tidb-mviewutil`), the view table from the SELECT's output types with its group key and `MaterializedViewInfo`, the owner's create step and its initial build, the refresh and refresh-source rows, and the rollback of a failed build. ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW (COMMENT, REFRESH with its schedule row, ATTRIBUTES) and DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW run as Go master's do too. The build chooses as Go master's does: IMPORT INTO ... FROM (definition) WITH Go's options on a TiKV store, REPLACE INTO on the embedded store (`buildCreateMaterializedViewData`); the TiKV path is unit-tested against Go's SQL but has not run on a real cluster. `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ... COMPLETE IN PLACE` runs as Go master's does (advisory lock, refresh-info row lock, history rows, DELETE + INSERT of the definition, refresh-source baseline, success persist, failure alert), and so does COMPLETE OUT OF PLACE (shadow table, build, cutover DDL, shadow cleanup) (its shadow loaded by IMPORT INTO on a TiKV store, `buildMVRefreshOutOfPlaceBuildSQL`); under the advisory lock a refresh reloads the node's schema when a committed DDL touches the view, its sources or their logs (`ensureMVRefreshSchemaVersion`, Go `TestMaterializedViewRefreshSchemaVersion`). Go master after this port's `eca4674a6f` baseline: nested materialized views (`27b1b52535f`: a ready view as a source, `validateMaterializedViewSourceState` / `validateMaterializedViewNestingDepth` / `validateMaterializedViewSourceMLog`, `ResolveFastRefreshSource`) are ported with Go's `mviewnested` create, column (their `worker` modes through a test hook that keeps a statement's job for a later `do_ddl_job_wrapper`, Go's `ExecutorForTest`), purge, refresh and refresh-source tests; `36b2c7f57ec` (OUT OF PLACE refresh of a view with its own log or dependent views: the cutover replaces the log under a new ID, rebinds children, takes the log's purge advisory lock, and its delete-range, GC placement, notifier and stats handling) and `0a914c5b134` (errors 8182 / 8183) are ported with Go's `nested_oop_test` `ReplacesMLog` / `RebindsDependentMaterializedViews` and `TestGCPlacementRulesForMaterializedViewOutOfPlaceCutover`; so is its rollback-and-retry test, with Go's `mustRollbackTxnOnError` (an errored or cancelled step whose handler set it discards its session's statements too, a failed batched multi-schema sub-job included); its purge-concurrency test is ported (PURGE takes Go's `handleTableName` MDL on its target, and a write pins its base table's log, Go `tryLockMDLAndUpdateSchemaIfNecessary`), its concurrent-child test is ported, and its TiFlash-progress test is ported (Go's mock TiFlash keeps the placement rules its manager sets). `357915c30e7` (ADD COLUMN on a view's own log takes the view's refresh advisory lock, cancelling an unstarted job and not counting a started one's wait; OUT OF PLACE refuses a log mid-change; multi-schema sub-jobs run on the parent's worker session) is ported with Go's `TestAlterMaterializedViewLogAddColumnRefreshConflict` `RefreshLockLifetime` (with Go's `beforeWaitSchemaSynced`) and `PausedRejectsOutOfPlaceRefresh` (with Go's `afterDeliveryJob`). `6aec16d0234` (CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW [LOG] IF NOT EXISTS, the group-key index refusing DROP / RENAME / INVISIBLE, DROP TABLE of a shadow older than seven days) is ported and replayed from a Go master `2a6eb11aeb9` capture (its DM schema-tracker half has no counterpart here: the port has no schematracker). `61709c56ed4` (FLASHBACK CLUSTER refuses a materialized view or log in the current state or at the target, FLASHBACK TABLE refuses a view, log or shadow, current or dropped, and FLASHBACK DATABASE recovers at the drop's commit, restores the maintenance rows and rewrites view definitions naming a renamed schema) is ported with its `cluster_test` and `recovertest` tests; with it DROP DATABASE deletes its views' and logs' maintenance rows (Go master `f3f7b3bb4dd`) and the delete-range emulator honors Go's `EmulatorGCDisable`. A maintenance table this branch's bootstrap lacks holds no objects for the FLASHBACK CLUSTER check. COMPLETE DELTA APPLY (over FULL OUTER JOIN), PURGE MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG, CANCEL MATERIALIZED VIEW JOB with the task monitor, COMPARE MATERIALIZED VIEW and the SHOW forms run as Go master's do, and a user statement's writes to a view, its log or its shadow table are refused outside maintenance as Go master's are (`CheckMViewUpdatable` / `CheckMViewReadable`, ANALYZE's included). REFRESH ... DRY RUN and WITH PROFILE run as Go master's do. `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TIDB_MVIEWS`, `TIDB_MLOGS` and `TIDB_TABLE_MVIEW_DEPENDENCIES` (`bb23c552354`, with their predicate extractors and visibility rules) answer as Go master's do, replayed from Go master captures. FAST refresh runs as Go master's does (the planner's merge source over the log window with Go's commit-ts window estimate, the delta merge executor with MIN / MAX recomputed through the full-update index lookup, AS OF targets, the log baseline and integrity checks, its DRY RUN and PROFILE), and so does an AS OF refresh's MIN / MAX recompute, which reads the base table at the target (Go `FullUpdateSnapshot`, `TestMaterializedViewRefreshFastAsOfTimestampMinMaxTargetSnapshot`). `MAX_COUNT` / `MIN_COUNT` run as Go master's aggregates and window functions (`func_max_min_count.go`, window slide included) and parse as SQL functions under Go's builtin-token rule (replayed from a Go master capture). Go master's (`2a6eb11aeb9`) `pkg/executor/test/materializedview`, `pkg/ddl/tests/materializedview`, `pkg/ddl/tests/materializedviewlog`, `mviewnested` and `mviewoutputlog` tests all have same-named ports, and so do `materializedviewlog` purge's but `FinalizeFailureUsesWithoutCancel` (it cancels the statement's Go context, which this port's statement path has no counterpart for) and `mviewrefreshsource`'s but `SnapshotIdentity` and `ReadTSAfterRetry` (they need the refresh's snapshot-validation hooks and unistore's `pessimisticLockReturnWriteConflict`). `writetest`'s MLog write tests (47), `mview_worker_test.go` (`InitMViewSession` ported onto `SessionVars` with Go's `ApplyMViewExecutionSessionVarsWithConfig`, which refresh, compare and the observe session now call; but `InitCreateMaterializedViewBuildSessionAppliesDefinitionDivPrecisionIncrement`: the DDL build session still takes its variables as a list) and `planner/mview` (but `ValidateCompleteDiffSelectFieldsNil`: a parsed SELECT always has its field list) have same-named ports; `planner/mview` is transcreated in Go's structure (`buildLocal` / `buildFromLocal` and each SELECT builder, Go's `HandleCols`), with each SELECT written as SQL and the nested builders' trees joined as Go's are. `casetest/mview` has its mock-schema plan and EXPLAIN tests ported (`casetest_mview_tests.rs`); Go builds the refresh plans in the planner where this tier builds them at execution through the executor's planner bridge (its optimizer lives there), with the same plans and EXPLAIN rows. `pkg/executor/mviewdeltamergeagg` is transcreated as `tidb-executor-mviewdeltamergeagg` with its 38 tests (and `pkg/executor/internal/util`'s `MarkTouchedRowsByColumn`), and FAST refresh runs it, built as Go's `mview_delta_merge_agg_builder.go` builds it (`driver/mview_delta_merge_agg_builder.rs`: the agg mappings, the MIN / MAX batch recompute over the index join, the log-aware target table writer, its runtime stats). `casetest/mview`'s `AsOfTimestampPlanWithMinMaxCarriesFullUpdateSnapshot` is ported beside them, and its two for-update-TS cases (`UsesForUpdateTSForUnboundedRefresh`, `ObtainsForUpdateTSWhenNotProvided`) run over a session (`materialized_view/casetest.rs`): FAST refresh takes Go's `GetStmtForUpdateTS` from the statement's store (`stmt_for_update_ts`). `pkg/mvservice`'s unit tests are ported under Go's names (100 of 101; `TestTimeProxyInstallPanicWhenModuleNil` has no Rust form, the installer takes an `Arc`), and Go's MV log analysis (`AnalyzeMVLog`, `LoadAllTiDBMVLogAnalyzeTasks`) and `RegisterMVService` live in `tidb-mvservice` as in Go, the domain passing its statistics handle, process tracker and server views. This branch's bootstrap does not create Go master's five materialized view tables (`mysql.tidb_mview_refresh_info` .. `tidb_mlog_purge_hist`, Go master's `upgradeToVer316`). The mview background service (`pkg/mvservice`) runs as Go master's does (scheduled FAST refresh and log purge, MV log auto-analyze, history GC, refresh alerts, accumulation counts, its sysvars). IMPORT INTO depends on them in one place: a next-gen IMPORT INTO ... FROM SELECT runs on a DXF worker (`ImportStepQuery`) only during materialized-view maintenance (`InMViewMaintenance`), so this port refuses every next-gen FROM SELECT, as Go does outside maintenance, and `ImportStepQuery` is not ported.
